qa_pairs.question: What are the considerations when using the `-O3` optimization level with the GCC compiler?
qa_pairs.answer: The `-O3` option in the GCC compiler may include optimizations that are potentially unsafe for certain types of code, such as code that relies on aliasing. If there is uncertainty, it is recommended to use the `-O2` option instead. Users can also consult the `man g++` page to identify and disable specific unsafe optimizations enabled by `-O3`.

qa_pairs.question: What is an important consideration regarding the C++ ABI when linking with GCC, especially when using different compiler versions?
qa_pairs.answer: The C++ Application Binary Interface (ABI) is frequently updated, and major compiler releases, such as the transition from GCC 4.9 to 5.1, can introduce significant ABI changes. If all source code and dependent libraries are recompiled with the same compiler version, there are usually no issues. However, if linking to older, precompiled binaries or libraries built with a different compiler version, an ABI mismatch may cause linking to fail. In such cases, GCC's Dual ABI feature can be used; for example, passing `-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0` to GCC v5.1 or higher will instruct it to use the old ABI for compatibility.

qa_pairs.question: How can users ensure standards-compliant floating-point support when compiling code with Intel C/C++ compilers?
qa_pairs.answer: Intel C/C++ compilers may default to using floating-point optimizations that are potentially unsafe. To ensure ANSI/ISO/IEEE standards-compliant floating-point support, users should consult the Intel man pages (e.g., `man icpc`) and are recommended to use one of two specific options: `-fp-model precise` or `-fp-model source`.
